records.name: Kerala
records.summary:
The state holds a constituted Transgender Welfare Board - one of the 12 states/UTs reported to the federal parliament in December 2021 as having set one up under the national trans-protection rules - and its law-enforcement machinery is measurably engaged: the state registered 2 of the 7 national cases under the Transgender Persons Act in 2021 and 4 of the 11 recorded in 2023, among the highest sub-national totals in those years.

That activity should be read with the source's own caveat: national recording is sparse (20 cases across 2019-23) because of police registration bias, against survey data showing 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence prevalence. Registered cases therefore evidence a system that at least accepts complaints, not rarity of violence. No state-specific restriction is documented; for a trans visitor the picture is one of institutional recognition machinery in a state where such machinery exists and is used.

sources.summary: Queerbeat crime-data report (30 Jan 2026), Kerala rows: 2 of the 7 national Transgender Persons Act cases in 2021 and 4 of the 11 in 2023 (joint-highest with Tamil Nadu) — among the highest sub-national totals, with the report's caveat that national counts are tiny from police-registration bias.

PIB federal reply (Dec 2021): Kerala is among the 12 states/UTs reported to parliament as having constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under Section 10(1) of the 2019 Rules — the named-board claim the record summary rests on.

records.name: Assam
records.summary:
Assam appears in national crime records with 2 of the 7 cases registered under the Transgender Persons Act in 2021, and none in the 2023 tally - the source itself cautions that national counts are tiny (20 cases 2019-23) because of police registration bias, with 2025 survey data showing 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence prevalence nationally. Recorded cases prove the complaint system is reachable, not that violence is uncommon.

In the December 2021 national government reply listing the 12 states/UTs that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards, Assam is not among them - no state welfare machinery stood in place as of that date. No state-specific protective or restrictive statute, ordinance or checkpoint operation is documented in the audited sources; the record supports a thin official-visibility finding for a trans visitor, balanced against the region-wide caveats, nothing more.

sources.summary: Queerbeat crime-data report (30 Jan 2026), Assam rows: 2 of the 7 Transgender Persons Act cases registered nationally in 2021 fell in Assam, none in the 2023 tally — complaint system reachable; report cautions national counts are tiny (20 cases 2019-23) due to police-registration bias, with 2025 survey prevalence at 27.2% physical / 22.3% sexual violence.

PIB federal reply (Dec 2021): the reply to parliament names the 12 states/UTs that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under the 2019 Rules — Assam is absent from that list, evidencing the record's 'no state welfare machinery as of Dec 2021' claim.
